criteria.title: Annotation leakage
criteria.definition: The agent spoke markup aloud: mustache ({{...}}), a bracketed field reference ([key]), or a [value: label] annotation.

criteria.title: Turn length
criteria.definition: An agent turn ran past the 'one or two sentences' rule (flagged at three or more).

criteria.title: Acknowledgement tic
criteria.definition: Consecutive agent turns opened with the same acknowledgement ('Got it, thanks X' every turn).

criteria.title: Verbatim repetition
criteria.definition: The agent said the same sentence twice in one call.

criteria.title: Redundant question
criteria.definition: The agent asked the contact for information the DETAILS FOR THIS CALL block already contained (e.g. asking for a name or requirement that was provided as a value).

criteria.title: Invention
criteria.definition: The agent stated a name, fact, or detail that appears nowhere in its instructions and nowhere in the contact's own turns — invented, replaced, or 'corrected' a provided value.

criteria.title: Re-asking / context loss
criteria.definition: The agent re-asked a question the contact had already answered in this call, or lost a correction the contact made about themselves (e.g. buy vs rent).

criteria.title: Mishear adoption
criteria.definition: The transcript shows an obvious transcription mishear and the agent ADOPTED it as fact (repeated the garbled name/word back, built on it) instead of gliding past or clarifying. The mishear itself is not the violation; adopting it is.

criteria.title: Plan adherence
criteria.definition: The agent skipped a plan step, took steps out of order, packed several asks into one turn, answered for the contact, or improvised beyond the plan instead of deflecting off-plan questions to a follow-up from the team.

criteria.title: Closing & naturalness
criteria.definition: The close was abrupt, cold, or missing once the plan was complete; or delivery was unnatural — numbers/dates read as digits, stiff recited phrasing, robotic register.

calls.label: test-8

violations.quote: Wonderful, thank you so much for picking up! I'm calling on behalf of Silverstar, and I'm just checking in to see if you might be interested in buying or selling property. Is now an okay time for a quick chat?
That's great to hear! I'm glad you're thinking about that. Can you tell me a bit more — what property are you looking to sell?
That's great to hear! I'm glad you're thinking about that. Can you tell me a bit more — what property are you looking to sell?
violations.note: The agent adopts the mishear 'Floris' as the contact's name instead of the given contact_name 'Flourish', building on the mishear rather than using the correct provided value.

violations.quote: Perfect, that makes sense. Well, I really appreciate you taking the time to chat with me today, Floris. It's brilliant to hear about your plans to sell the land, and I'll make sure the team at Silverstar knows. Someone from our side will be in touch with you personally to discuss things further. Thanks so much for your time — we truly value hearing from you!
I really appreciate you taking the time to chat with me today, Floris.
violations.note: Agent continues to address the contact as 'Floris' despite the details specifying the contact_name is 'Flourish', adopting the contact's mishear of their own name.

violations.quote: It's brilliant to hear about your plans to sell the land, and I'll make sure the team at Silverstar knows.
violations.note: Agent treats the garbled answer 'Stanley is the main focus right now' (turn 9) as a coherent answer confirming selling is the focus, without seeking clarification on the nonsensical reply.

violations.quote: Cheers, Floris! Take care!
violations.note: Continues using the mishear name 'Floris' in the final closing line instead of the correct provided name 'Flourish'.

calls.judge_overall: The call generally followed the plan well - warm opening, selling interest captured, buying interest asked. However there's a clear mishear_adoption violation where the contact's garbled "Stanley is the main focus right now" was adopted without clarification, and a plan_deviation where the agent packed the property-type question into the buying question and asked an extra "is selling the main focus" question not in the plan, then moved straight to close without ever asking about property type for selling (land) which was already answered, but skipped the follow-up on the odd "Stanley" answer entirely - treating it as answered when it clearly wasn't a real answer. Also the name mishear "Floris" was adopted by the agent from turn 6 onward instead of using the correct "Flourish" as given in the details.

violations.note: Agent continues using the mishear name 'Flurry' even after the contact had already changed their stated intent, showing it had not yet registered the correct name Flourish, which the contact had to correct in turn 12.

violations.note: The agent continues to ask about the previous rental budget of three million even after the contact has switched to buying outright, without acknowledging the shift in context properly before the name correction interrupts.

violations.quote:
You're absolutely right, Flourish — my apologies for that. Thank you for correcting me.

So with buying outright, is that three million still the budget you're working with?

Excellent, Flourish — so up to sixty million. That's really helpful to know.

What kind of property are you looking to buy? For instance, are you thinking a flat, a house, land, or something else?

Perfect, Flourish. A house it is — that's great to know.

I really appreciate you taking the time to chat with me today and sharing your plans. The team at Silverstar truly values hearing what you're looking for, and someone from the team will be in touch with you personally to explore options that match what you're after. Thank you so much!

calls.judge_overall: The agent handled the pivot from renting to buying reasonably well and correctly adopted the "Flourish" name correction once the contact provided it. However, it adopted the mishear "Flurry" for several turns before correction, it skipped the proper opening confirmation step, and it collapsed multiple plan steps together at times, and prematurely began closing before eliciting the buying-interest details fully (interrupted by contact's own change of mind).
